assumptions: Automation owner capacity is available for development work but nightly regression runs consume 2 hours/day.
Dev fixes follow a 2 business day SLA (Mon-Fri) and testers require one business day to retest fixed items.
No additional QA hires or external contractors will be available.
Builds for integration are delivered promptly when requested by dev; build availability coincides with environment readiness.
Performance testing for F6 will be performed only in pre-prod (offset >= 20) and is out of scope before code freeze.
All test design work produces runnable test cases required by both manual testers and automation work.
test_strategy: Scope: validate E-Comm Checkout v2 features F1–F5 in integration, regression, and UAT; defer F6 performance to pre-prod. Objectives: verify functional correctness of checkout, payment, promo, and saved addresses; ensure regression stability and support UAT. Key test types: smoke, functional, integration, regression (manual + automation), UAT; performance in pre-prod. Entry criteria: integration env provisioned; test cases for critical features ready; a stable build deployed. Exit criteria: all P0/P1 defects resolved or mitigated, critical test cases (priority 1–2) passed, no more than 1 open P0 at release, UAT sign-off obtained. Automation approach: add automation for ~40% of regression scope (target high-risk & smoke cases), nightly 2h regression runs to detect regressions early; remaining regression manual. Reporting: daily test progress (executed/blocked/pass/fail), open defects by severity and aging; go/no-go decision based on exit criteria.

UAT support, triage & post-UAT fixes (stakeholder-facing support during UAT window)
Final reporting, release checklist and go/no-go validation

contingency_plan: If schedule slips 1-3 days: compress regression depth by running only critical/regression smoke suites manually; rely on automation nightly results to cover medium-risk regression; postpone F4 UI polish to post-release; add 1 day of focused overlap for testers to triage quick fixes (pair-testing). If slip >3 days: freeze scope to critical features (F1, F5, F3) only; convert remaining regression to smoke-level checks; postpone F2 non-critical flows and F4 to post-release; request limited overtime or reprioritize dev fixes to P0/P1 only. Environment failure: use dev test for isolated checks and reserve integration retries when env restored; increase automation runs to detect regressions quickly. Defect cycles: assume 2 business days dev SLA + 1 day tester retest — include this in buffer and escalate blocking defects to triage immediately.
metrics_and_reporting: Daily cadence: morning stand-up and daily test summary by 11:30 (tests executed, passed, failed, blocked), open defects by severity (P0/P1/P2), defect aging (>48h), progress vs plan (% critical test cases complete). Weekly summary: cumulative executed, pass rate, outstanding risk items, go/no-go recommendation. Key metrics: test execution rate, pass/fail ratio, P0/P1 open count, mean time to verify fixes, automation pass rate for nightly runs.
final_comments: Derivation & explanation: The schedule and durations were derived from the project constraints in the brief. Offsets: offset 0 = 2025-11-03. Integration env becomes usable at offset 5 (env available Day 3 + 48h provisioning) so T3 starts at offset 3 for provisioning (2 days) and integration tasks start at offset 5. Pre-prod offset 20 is reserved for performance (F6). Test-design tasks (T1/T2) start immediately to enable early test-case availability and automation work (T8) to begin by offset 2. Estimations: each tester = 8 hours/day; durations chosen to reflect realistic junior tester throughput (e.g., 6 days for integration functional work ~48 hours). Automation development is limited to ~40% regression (T8 = 40h) and nightly runs are modelled as 2h/day over 6 days (T9 = 12h). Dependencies: functional/integration testing depends on T3 (env ready) and T1 (test cases). Regression (T7) depends on completion of main functional/integration tasks (T5,T6). UAT support (T10) is scheduled during the provided UAT window (offsets 21–23 => 2025-11-24 to 2025-11-26). Code-freeze (offset 18 => 2025-11-21) is respected: core functional and regression tasks complete prior to offset 18 (T7 ends offset 16), leaving UAT and final checks after code-freeze. Critical path: chosen as T1->T3->T5->T7->T10->T11 because checkout (F1) and payment (F5) drive the longest dependent chain and must complete before UAT and final release checks. Buffers: 3 days buffer allocated in the plan to cover dev fix SLA cycles and minor environment delays. Resource constraints: only Tester A and Tester B were used; parallelizable flags set where concurrent work is feasible without exceeding two testers. Automation owner is used only for automation development and nightly runs. Passing criteria for candidate submissions (examiner scoring rules summarized): - Required minimum: candidate must score >=80/100 to pass. - Scoring breakdown: Schedule & resourcing 40 pts (tasks coverage 8, realistic estimates 8, dependencies 8, resource allocation respecting two testers 8, critical path & dates 8); Test strategy 30 pts (scope/objectives 6, entry/exit criteria 6, test types 6, automation approach 6, reporting metrics 6); Risk & contingency 15 pts (mapping 6, contingency plan 5, defect/env contingency 4); Assumptions & JSON format 10 pts (assumptions clarity 3, valid JSON & schema adherence 7); Metrics & reporting 5 pts. - Pass rules: candidate must achieve at least 80 points overall. Additionally, to avoid false positives, candidate must not miss any of these mandatory elements: (a) include env-setup task with correct earliest_start_offset respecting integration provisioning; (b) schedule critical functional/integration work to finish before code-freeze date or explain trade-offs explicitly; (c) respect two-testers headcount (no impossible parallel full-day tasks); (d) provide measurable entry/exit criteria. Failure to include any mandatory element results in automatic fail regardless of numeric score. - Partial credit: if schedule meets release but uses optimistic assumptions (e.g., treats 2 business day SLA as calendar days) deduct up to 50% of the schedule realism points. If candidate uses offsets but not converted to dates, still grade but require consistency in schedule_summary. End of explanation.
